instruction: Do the new shift rules in Major League Baseball make the game more exciting?
reference: Prior to this season, Major League Baseball(MLB) allowed infielders to shift based on who was at bat for the opposing team. The shift simply means that the defending infield could load a certain side of the infield. For example, the shortstop could move to where the 2nd baseman normally is positioned and the 2nd baseman might play in shallow right field. The 3rd baseman would occupy the left side of the infield. The theory behind this shift strategy is based on advanced analytics used in the game of baseball. Using a spray chart to determine where a hitter normally puts a ball in play and with what type of pitch thrown, the defending team would shift to cover more of the playing field and therefore increase the chance the defending team would record an out based on this strategy. It was increasingly used over the last 3-4 years and some argue that employing the shift decreased the number of hits and runs scored during a game. The downstream effect of this made for a lower scoring affair and a less exciting game for a fan base that is increasingly younger and looking for more excitement during baseball games. One argument for allowing the shift is that hitters, being professionals, would adjust and try to beat the shift by hitting a ball away from the shift or hitting to the "opposite field." Hitters answer to beating the shift was to increase their launch angle and play for the home run. While the home run was an important run scoring mechanism, MLB decided to outlaw the shift from defensive strategy for the 2023 season. Hitters refusal to adjust to the shift led to this decision by MLB. The concern was games were not action packed enough and ultimately MLB would continue to lose popularity by its younger viewers, opting for other sports like Basketball, Football, or Hockey to spend their money on. No longer can you sift defensive players. The rules for this season are there must be 2 defenders on each side of 2nd base and their feet must be on the infield dirt as the pitch is being delivered. The hope is more hits will be produced, more runs scored, and an increase in fan approval created. The early opinion after the first week of the MLB season is that the games are proving to be faster paced with more runs and all around action created.

instruction: Write me a recursive function for calculating the nth fibonacci number
reference: Below is a recursive Python function fib(n) that computes the nth Fibonacci number. This is split into a base case and a recursive case. The base case is given by the fact that the first two terms of the Fibonacci sequence are 0 and 1, so fib(0)=0 and fib(1)=1. The recursive case is given by the fact that the nth Fibonacci number f_n can be written as the sum of the previous two Fibonacci numbers, so f_n = f_{n-1} + f_{n-2}. Putting this all together, we get ``` def fib(n): # base case if n == 0: return 0 if n == 1: return 1 # recursive case return fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2) ``` This will correctly calculate the nth Fibonacci number for nonnegative integer inputs n. However, recursively calculating Fibonacci numbers in this way takes exponential time in the value of n, so this code may be very slow for large inputs. It could be improved by memoizing previous results, or using a non-recursive approach. Simple iterative approaches can solve the problem more quickly, and closed-form expressions for the nth Fibonacci number exist and are even faster to evaluate.

instruction: If you found yourself washed up on a deserted tropical island with no hope for immediate rescue, what would you do?
reference: The immediate first step is to ensure you are not materially injured. Assuming your only manifestation of harm is a psychological roller coaster of fear, anger and hopelessness, your best course of action is to attend to your basic needs first. Locate a protected space away from the wind but not too deep into the surrounding jungle, built a fire pit and gather enough combustable materials to carry you through the first few evenings. Find fresh water and someway to hold it (open coconut shells / fashioned palm leave bowls etc) - DO NOT DRINK IT until you boil it first over your new fire so you mitigate the risk of getting sick. Before your first nightfall with secure fire and water taken care of, build yourself a make shift shelter so you are protected from the elements and yet to be discovered critters. Day two, focus your energies gathering food (coconuts / seaweed / clams etc) so you keep your energy high. Once your very basic needs are met (shelter / water / food to survive), its time to fashion a fishing pole and a sharp spear out of bamboo so you can fish and hunt for birds to expand your food sources. Day three, focus your energy on building yourself a more permanent shelter. Explore the island for wood and rock sources; along with large palm leave you can fashion rope from. While exploring your new home, look for caves and / or places where you could construct a tree fort so you can improve your protected living space. Week 2, once your new living quarters are secured and you have sustainable methods to care for your basic needs, climb to the highest point of the island and look for nearby islands / land and any indication of human habitation. While searching for these indicators, assess methods of island escape to get through any surf and start tracking wind and weather patterns daily so you can get a feel for the seasonal rotations. Week 3 +, dedicate 3-4 hours a day to building signal fires and SOS stone messages that overheard planes may be able to detect. It is also important to manage your mental health and track daily changes so you keep your sanity in check as you adjust to the new reality. Create a way to chronicle your experiences. One day you will escape your island and can sell your story to Hollywood. Of course, if you never do escape, you will at least have the comfort of leaving something behind for eventual discovery of proof you did survive the incident that landed you on this island.

instruction: Chatbot, please write an origin story for a character who is sort of a cross between a Cinderella princess and a superhero. She’s initially held by an evil witch but escapes and then meets some forest creatures who take her in to become their champion.

I was nearly ready to collapse by the time he stopped. “You are safe for now. You may rest with us.” To my surprise, I saw the dim figures of many animals around me. Not only deer but squirrels, boars, rabbits, beavers, and more. They chittered amongst themselves excitedly. At length, the stag spoke again. “Did you truly escape the Witch’s Tower? Under your own power?” It took time to find my voice. “Yes,” I said meekly. “It took a long time of looking for opportunities.” “Then you may be the one who was foretold. The great champion who will be our avatar in the human world.” Suddenly the creatures draped a heavy cloak over my shoulders and an antlered helmet upon my head. “You will defend the forest from those who would do it harm and enlist the good peoples of the human world to battle evil. instruction: Write me a paragraph explaining why Dodo birds went extinct.

instruction: What is the difference between a panster and a plotter? Is one better than the other? I am writing a blog post on it, but for right now I just wasnt some brief tips so I can research further. For now, just a couple of paragraphs is fine, I just need something to get me going.
reference: A panster writes "by the seat of their pants". They start with a general idea, or maybe even just a character, and just let the story go where their imagination goes. Stephen King, Diana Gabaldon, and George R.R. Martin are great examples of pansters. A plotter is a writer who outlines the story before they write a word of it. The most famous plotters are J.K. Rowling and James Patterson. Then, there are authors who combine a bit of both, like Agatha Christie. As far as what is best, it really depends on both the writer and the story. A panster may write an entire first draft without outlining. A plotter usually outlines everything first - settings, characters, scenes - and then starts writing. The drawback to pantsing is the writer might box themselves into a corner and need to re-write. The drawback to plotting is that as the story continues, the characters begin driving the story and tweaks need to be made. Genre is also a consideration, as it is much easier to pants science fiction than a mystery.

Finally, she was satisfied with her life. She was where she was meant to be, and she was going to enjoy putting on a show every week. -127

instruction: You are part of a small colony of humans 100 years into a 200 year interstellar mission. Due to the time passed, technology has allowed a new mission to exceed yours, and it sails past your ship but can not make contact
reference: **Exodus Log # 481 - Rotation # 20** *2132; 98 Years after Mission Start Date* Most of the crew is still in the Freezer. Well, actually, everyone except for me is still asleep, decided not to wake up the other Technician's after I saw the transmission from Earth. Unfortunately for everyone on board this ship, our leaders back on Earth have decided to send another mission to ION-4. They decided to dub it Exodus-2, as if the four hundred souls they sent on this mission have already returned or are already dead. We are not dead. And we are still 102 years from our destination. According to the transmission, we should be seeing Ex-2 any day now, even though they only left on their mission fifteen years ago. Technology has advanced at a rapid rate since we all left. Although we've been gone for 98 years, technology has moved jumped about 200 years. And unfortunately for us, they didn't account for this when they sent Ex-2 into the stars. Unfortunately for us, we'll get to watch Ex-2 fly by and reach ION-4 79 years faster than us. By the time we get there, everyone on board Ex-2 now will be dead, or in the final days of their life. And we'll be reaching a colony of their children. We'll be the eldest people on the planet, clocking in at 200 years older than anyone else. I, for one, am not looking forward to this. And I for one, am going to keep my crew in the Freezer for a few years longer than they anticipated. It's against regulation, but when the people who sent you on this mission 98 years ago, send a newer, fancier, and more technologically-advanced ship on the *same exact mission*, well, I think we can let regulation slide for a bit. I'm going to do the rounds, check on everyone's status, then watch Ex-2 flyby us. Without saying a damn word. Ex-2, if you're receiving this somehow, or hell if Earth can send this to you, I only have one thing to say. Tell your kids we're on our way. And we won't forget about them.

instruction: Stars have brilliant deaths, large explosions given a beautiful name. Men are granted nothing so glorious.
reference: They've been talking about it for billions of years now. The fact that we've made it this far is a credit to our race. We've seen glorious scientific triumphs, the fall of many great civilizations, and even times of peace. Today though, none of that matters anymore. The Sun was always only a battery, never a generator. No matter how many brilliant minds we put to the task we could never change that fact. Everyone around the planet is coming to terms with the end of the world in their own ways. Some are rioting. Others are at home quietly with their loved ones. Even more have ended their lives already in fear of what is about to happen. But none of that matters anymore. *Stars have brilliant deaths, large explosions given a beautiful name. Men are granted nothing so glorious. *

instruction: You thought learning the recorder in elementary school was some stupid music thing teachers made you do. It turns out they were training you for something else.
reference: We all thought the recorder was just some stupid instrument the teachers made us learn to " expand our experiences" We were wrong. No one could have predicted the war, but some how our teachers knew. All of that year learning, practicing, mastering the recorder would come back and save us. The machines, monsters, I don't know what to call them, they were invulnerable. Bullets could not stop them, explosions would not slow them down. We all thought hope was lost, but then the 9th grade Travis school kids came out. Formed rank and played. It was ugly, it sounded horrible, and it looked bad. But the music, no the noise, it overwhelmed our adversaries. It started to make them bleed and eventually weakened them and then we were able to win. That's why we learn to play the recorder. As a nod to our heritage and the war. " But mr Thomson, why doesn't Timmy have to learn" " Oh his parents gave him a note"

instruction: Our cause is righteous and just. We will not falter
reference: I recited the words, " Our cause is righteous and just. We will not falter," although I am the last one. For centuries I've stood guard in the same room. Many have tried to reach me, but all have failed. I remember the blistering sun of the desert, and the cool breeze of the Mediterranean. All else is becoming a faint memory. My daily routine of overseeing my treasures. That's what every man and woman have called the objects in my room. Little do they know that the word should be singular. Oh the treasures of this plain are worth quite a bit, but it is only the treasure of salvation that they should truly seek. I gaze into the small pool of water located in the center of my chamber. The echoes of another man screaming. Prey to another device. Maybe he doesn't know to kneel, or maybe he doesn't know how to spell. Some simply fall to their doom. More echoes. I've grown numb to the sounds of men dying. Even that of women. All I seek is the one to relinquish my duty. Footsteps. Those I have not heard since the time of Napoleon. In comes a man with a fedora on his head seeking the cup of a carpenter who took his name from the family dog.

instruction: When you drink from a water fountain, and you unknowingly become immortal. How did you find out and how did it affect your live?
reference: *F**k! This again. * You see, a funny thing happened to me on my way to work this morning. Well I say funny but it actually is quite the opposite, a gust of wind caught me mid umbrella-unfolding and then next thing you know, I'm in the middle of oncoming traffic and bam! I'm back in this cursed corridor, in my old awful high school next to the blasted water fountain. Have you ever been caught sneaking around a high school? During the school day? The day I slipped in the shower found me on the register, and not the kind you'd expect to find in a school. And oh, look! There is good old Mr. Jefferies and yup, he is calling the police. Oh and would you look at that it's recess. ^ (Hi kids! Don't do drugs!)... God I wish I did drugs. Y'know, I hate that water fountain. I hate that Mr. Jefferies and I hate the fact I was on my way to work as a photographer. *Yes you can confiscate the damn camera! * Well at least I know how I'm getting out of prison.

instruction: At the end of the year, a superhero receives a box in the mail from an anonymous journalist. reference: It took me hours to gather each of the obituaries. The flash drives weren't all that expensive, and each one held a few thousand obits. This so-called " hero" thinks that he's perfect, but he's just as flawed as everyone else. What I didn't expect to see what a reply. A small note appeared on my doorstep. If you thought that there were a lot of people that I couldn't save, wait until you see the number of people that I won't. I quit."

instruction: In 1907 Vienna Academy of Fine Arts rejects Young Adolf Hitler twice and soon after he survives four different assassination attempts by time travellers. Confused Hitler is convinced that its his art is what the world fears.

The world *will* like my art. I will see to it. It is my *destiny*.

instruction: Follow-up: You are a compulsive dancer. Anywhere there is music playing you struggle to remain still.
reference: The disease began with me. As far as I know, I was the first recorded case of it. In the beginning, friends and family thought it was a joke. The doctors thought me a liar. There was no possible scientific explanation for a disease that would make one dance, of all things, whenever music was heard. It just made no sense. But when we discovered that it was contagious, that I spread the disease wherever I went, the doctors started studying me seriously. Still, at the time it was still just a passing curiosity, and no hindrance to everyday life. The unease began when it turned out that the spread of the disease started to accelerate. The doctors, through careful experimentation, discovered that the disease had a delayed onset upon exposure. That countless many may have caught the disease without displaying the symptoms became cause for concern, and the doctors started working towards a cure. Then, finally, the terror began with the soft humming of a pop song. The music was heard everywhere, even in enclosed rooms, seemingly without a source. The city, as one, began to dance a subdued little jig. Following that, Beethoven's Ninth Symphony. If you are unfamiliar with this song, it is an hour long, quite dramatic and powerful. Accordingly, the people of the streets waltzed, forcefully. Twenty minutes in, the streets were panting and gasping from exertion. At the end of the song, screams for mercy were heard across the city. At that time, whatever cosmic DJ that staged this impromptu dance party decided that the warm-up was over. It began to play its own unending mix of heavy metal and dubstep. And oh how the city learned to hate these two genres. Between the headbanging and moshing, the screams ended. There was no breath left in the people to scream. The city fell, one by one, out of heart attacks, strokes, exhaustion. The weakest among us died within half an hour of the mad dance. The strongest began collapsing after the third hour. And I? I managed to crush the auditory organs in my ears through a particularly inventive method of headbanging, along with parts of my skull. And as I lay bleeding and dying, I looked out into the crowd and cursed the cruel and twisted world that would come up with the terrible and silly idea of compulsive dancing.

instruction: A soldier in the heat of battle suddenly hears a voice that says " I am your child's imaginary friend. They have sent me to protect you in your greatest time of need. "
reference: Sergeant Coleman of the SAS had seen more than his fair share of battle. Yet ambushes were something even the elite can't always prepare for, his convoy as testament upon erupting in a series of explosions, but as it did, a voice rumbled into existence. " I am your daughters what you would call'imaginary' friend, and she made me promise to protect you, but it comes with a price" The voice was rasp but distinct, like it reverberated off the skull, intertwining with the rattles of gunfire and shelling. Coleman lay untouched next to the wreck of his vehicle, all occupants but him dead inside. Assessing the situation, their convoy came under attack from both IEDs and RPGs, with the explosions sending all vehicles in different directions, how he survived was a mystery. Doubled with hearing voices he thought he was dead, until a stray bullet glanced his arm and the white hot burn snapped him back to reality. " Wh.. what? Who are you?" " Who I am is not important, whether you wish to survive is. Three approaching your six, Sergeant" There it was again, whether it was the shell shock or his comms he couldn't tell, didn't care as he spun into cover as bullets whizzed by overhead, exactly where he was standing just moments before. " God damn it, I don't care the cost just get me out of here!" Assessing his options, Coleman saw two points of cover, sandbags or a building. Whilst blindly firing into the hills, the voice returned... " The building, might want to use one of those grenades of yours, run quickly now..." The voice trailed off as Coleman burst out of cover. The sand kicked and danced around him as he sprinted to the house and threw the frag inside. The resulting screams sent a shiver down his spine. How did whatever was helping him know? Bursting through the door the damage was already done, through the window he saw the sandbags get hit by a stray mortar, and explode upwards in a spray of sand and dust. " Delta squad under attack! I repeat!" The soft crackle confirmed his radios demise, just as an enemy silhouette materialised in front of the door with his gun raised. " Click, click, click..... Click" Four dead man's clicks? What were the odds? Coleman thought as he sunk two in his enemies chest. Suddenly he realised his wasn't the only presence. " You humans and your odds and chances, no you must live this day, for I forever keep my promises as you must keep yours..." It trailed off again, this time the vibration in his head seemed to finally leave, yet as he watched from the window the enemy emplacements misfired sending explosions all across the mountainside. Coleman reached for the photo of his daughter, and found a burn where her face used to be. " What have I done?"

instruction: In the near future, mankind explores the stars in search of life. Life indeed exists beyond Earth, but you, a researcher on a science ship, discover that all of the spacefaring alien civilizations died out. Curiously, their deaths seem directly linked to humanity reaching outer space.
reference: They found it on Proxima Centauri. A stele six meters high by two meters wide, covered by an inscription obviously linguistic but totally foreign. They brought it home. After six years, a team of MIT scientists announced the code was cracked. The world gathered to hear its meaning, to hear the words of extraterrestrials long extinct. Geologists invented a new kind of carbon dating to test its age, a necessary task to probe the alien materials inside. They dated it at 4 billion years old. What struck the explorers more than anything was the cleanliness of the ruins they kept finding. It appeared that the inhabitants disappeared only recently. Some pointed to self-cleaning materials. Others insisted that the'cities' were mere outposts left behind. The WHO's epidemiologists insisted it showed all he telltale signs of a massive plague. Their theory gained credence when a high-resolution satellite photo of the arctic facility on Io revealed a chunk of space debris the size of a four door sedan embedded in a wall. The letters on the side were undeniably Soviet. A long lost relic of the Cold War, a century before. The world gathered to hear the words of these ancients. A squirrelly looking man in a black suit and wire-framed glasses took the podium, and the earth held its breath. " The inscription reads," he started, "'The contagion has been contained on a blue planet, third from the sun. Planet is devoid of life and inhospitable. The rebuilding must now begin."

instruction: You wake up in a dimly lit prison cell to find your cell door busted open, a pile of unconscious guards, a stuffed duck called Leeroy, the faint sound of Gangnam Style, and an absurd amount of blood on your hands
reference: " Why am I dreaming about Koreans?" I wonder as I regain maybe 1/4 consciousness from sleep. The air smells of ozone. And damp iron. I can hear a fluorescent light blinking rapidly on and off, trying to ignite the gas inside. Gangnam Style is barely making its way to my ears. " What the fuck?" I open my eyes. I'm staring at a ceiling I don't recognize. My blood runs cold and I sit upright with a jolt, eyes wide. I'm in a prison cell? I think. It's dark outside so no light is coming in from the slim window. The only light is coming from the faint and noisy flickering of a cheap fluorescent light above and what's coming in from the hallway outside. There is a steel door that is mangled to a degree that I can't fathom what in the hell could have caused its current shape. It's pushed inwards and the paint has come off where something struck it. Most of the paint that has come off has been replaced with what I'm sure is blood. A shoe lies in the view out the door from the bed. " So you're up." I let out a short scream like a girl and look around. There's no one. " Over here..." I look around. On the bookshelf is a stuffed animal. A duck. " On the shelf. Name's Leroy." " Yeah, I'm not fucking with any of this." I say and I lay back down, pull the sheets up and close my eyes. " Wake up, idiot!" A soft thud hits the floor. I open one eye and cast it towards the sound. The stuffed duck is on the floor looking at me. " Fuck off, duck." I close my eye again. " Leroy. And that won't work. Besides, we need to move before the guards who miraculously have survived regain consciousness and lock this place back down." " What?" The duck just blankly stared in my direction. " What?" No answer. I sit up. I pinch myself and recoil from myself as I notice blood *everywhere* on my hands and I hear a sigh from the floor. I look over at the duck. " Where am I? What's going on?" Still no answer. If I'm dreaming I'm not going to wake up by going to sleep in it so I swing my legs off the bed and stand up, bending down to pick up the duck I hear over the intercom, " All guards to cellblock B immediately. Secure the area at all costs!" I look at my door. Cell B-14. I poke my head around the corner of the doorway and onto the gangway. It is littered with guards and I can see flashlight beams far away heading towards me. Whatever is coming that way I have a feeling isn't going to be pleasant. " Run." Leroy says to me.

instruction: An atheist and a Satanist meet at the gates of heaven. Saint Peter says there's only room for one of them.

instruction: You're at a pub when you see an attractive woman sitting alone at a table, after you approach her and talk for a while you hit it off; only to find out that she is there to meet someone she met online.
reference: She batted her eyes at me, " You know, you're not bad." She spoke slowly so I would hang on every word, " In fact, you're doing really well at this whole'bar date' thing." It was good to hear, most times on these I've crashed and burned, " well, I'm good at a lot of other things too." I looked into her eyes and she looked back into mine. " I've heard a silver tongue can be very versatile." Un-fucking-believable. The woman he eyed was a voluptuous blonde with deep blue eyes and a clear complexion. She wore a tight dress that ended above her knees. She was the hottest woman at the bar. I had never had someone flirt with me like this on the first time meeting. Since the beginning, they had been flirting. Finally, I said: " You wouldn't even believe, it's mind blowing." " You know," she began, " I don't think you're a socially awkward penguin in the slightest." What. Roll with it. " Well, at the end of the day I am a human." " So, what, you told me you're bad at conversation. I think you're phenomenal. I only thought you were witty online, where everyone has minutes to think about what they say. Yet here you are, flirting like a champion. Are you gon na take me home, penguin?" "... Penguin?" " Tell me your real name, and don't say James Bond." " Joe." " Alright,'Joe,' I'll fold. I've been attracted to you before we even met here. The third night we talked I knew I was going to meet you. Do I meet your expectations?" Shit. She thinks I'm someone else. " Oh." I felt disappointed. This woman was drop-dead gorgeous and it had almost happened. " Well, listen, let me be honest- I don't think I'm who you think I am. " Well, you look like your picture. Thanks for not cat-fishing me, by the way. You're handsome." My god, I look just like this guy. " Well, I'm not the guy you met. Maybe a happy coincidence." " Oh my god," she said, " What the hell? Look at me, I'm hot! You're going to pretend this isn't you?" She pulled out her phone and looked through it a bit before stopping and turning it towards me. There, staring right back at me was my facebook profile picture.

instruction: The protagonist often breaks the 4th wall, and so the narrator decides to break the 5th. Things are getting heated between the two.
reference: Yo, me again. It's the Protagonist. The guy who actually has to live out everything you people write. And, uh, this prompt is weird. See, oftentimes I *am* the narrator. This is one of those times. I guess I'm a masochist or whatever. So, enough talking to you, here's today's story. Woke up, drank coffee, went to the postmodernist dreamscape where all fictional characters go to perform their stories, yadda yadda. Anyway, so I was supposed to be acting out Deadpool today, but something went wrong. I was about to start, I had my lines ready. There was an excellent fourth wall break in my mind. I braced myself. It was time to run. I dashed forward with everything I had in me. The fourth wall was made of bricks, and it wasn't going to break easily. Still, I had to do it. The plot wants what the plot wants. As soon as I hit the wall, however, I knew I had made a mistake. This was not the brick of the fourth wall, or the curtain of the second, or even the bamboo paper of the first and third walls. As I crashed through the wall, splinters punctured my skin. The characteristic wood of the fifth wall gave way, and I entered a room of pure white. I fell to the floor, my vision blurry. I turned around to see the set disappeared, endless white filling my sight. In the distance I saw a blotch of brown, an oasis of color in this expanse of nothing. I made my way toward it with little hope of ever getting out of this realm. My vision cleared, and I saw a table. Upon it lied a pen and paper. A way out! I quickly scribbled down a story, crafting an escape from this nightmare. _______________________________________________________ Part 2 soon

instruction: You are a consort to the king of a kingdom at war. The king goes off to battle, but doesn't return. After the battle, two priests from a nearby shrine ask you to help them identify the king's body on the battlefield.
reference: " Will you help us?" The white-robed men had asked. " Will you help us to find your husband's body?" His *body. * His cold, pale, ghastly corpse - no doubt covered in blood. *His* blood. The blood of this enemies. His soldiers. His comrades... " No," the Queen whispered - more to herself than to the two men who stood before her - " No, I can not! I could not bear to see him-" *Dead... * He *can't* be dead... The Queen's knobby, white-knuckled hands tightened around the armrests of her throne. She stared down, at her dress, at the great stone steps, at *anything* that was not the empty throne beside her. " Please!" The elder priest begged her, falling to his knees. " *Please, * give us your aid! It is only right that we bring the King back to his castle, so that he may be properly buried and given peace. You are the only one who can help us to identify him!" The King had always been a very stern and solitary man. Rarely did he ever leave his study. Always plotting and planning and worrying... and drinking.
